<explanation>
Below is a set of tailored guidelines for producing a clear, accurate system-design diagram for the Interview_DS_Algo repository.  Although it isn’t a “web app” or microservices platform, you can still capture its essential architecture as a content‐distribution and development ecosystem.  Follow these steps:

1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a large, topic-wise code repository for data-structures and algorithms interview prep.  
   - It contains C++ solutions organized into folders like Arrays, Graph, DP, etc., plus a top-level README that explains the repository’s mission, contributor model, and external links (YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn).  

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level directories represent algorithm domains (e.g., Arrays/, Graph/, DP/, …).  
   - Each domain folder has many subfolders sometimes further subdivided by pattern (e.g., DP/1-D DP/, Graph/BFS_DFS/, etc.).  
   - There's no build script or service folder—just code files and Markdown docs.  
   - The README.md at the root describes the content and links to social media.  

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - No mention of a runtime server; the project is purely static code + documentation.  
   - External dependencies are only embed links (YouTube videos, social profiles), no databases or back-end APIs.  

4. Main components to represent  
   a. Local Development Environment  
      - Developers clone the Git repo, browse folders in their IDE (e.g., VS Code), compile individual .cpp solutions, run tests locally.  
   b. Version Control & CI/CD Platform  
      - GitHub (central repo) holds the code.  
      - (Optionally) GitHub Actions or another CI can be introduced to run style checks, compile‐and‐test each folder, or generate documentation.  
   c. Documentation & Publishing  
      - The Markdown files (README.md and per-folder READMEs) are rendered by GitHub’s UI.  
      - Optionally a static-site generator (e.g., MkDocs, Docusaurus) could consume the Markdown and produce a hosted site on GitHub Pages.  
   d. External Services  
      - YouTube for embedded video tutorials.  
      - Social links (Facebook page, LinkedIn group).  

5. Relationships / Data flow  
   - Developer → Git push/PR → GitHub central.  
   - GitHub Actions (CI) triggered on push → compiles & tests code → artifacts (e.g., generated docs).  
   - Docs published to GitHub Pages → end users browse online.  
   - README embeds YouTube videos; browser fetches content from YouTube.  

6. Architectural patterns & principles  
   - “Content-repository” pattern: code and docs together.  
   - Separation of concerns:  
     • Code module layers (by algorithm category)  
     • Documentation layer (Markdown)  
     • Publishing layer (static-site or GitHub UI)  
   - Extensibility: new algorithm folders can be added without changing the CI/CD pipeline.  

7. Guidelines for the diagram  
   - Use rectangular boxes for each component:  
     • Local Dev (IDE + Compiler)  
     • GitHub Repo (with sub-boxes for Code Modules and Docs)  
     • CI/CD Service  
     • Static-Site Generator / Publishing Service  
     • End Users (browsers)  
     • External Video Service (YouTube)  
   - Draw directional arrows:  
     • From Local Dev to GitHub (push)  
     • From GitHub to CI/CD (trigger)  
     • From CI/CD to Publishing Service (artifact export)  
     • From End Users to Publishing Service (HTTP GET)  
     • From End Users to YouTube (video embed fetch)  
   - Color-code:  
     • Developer tools (blue)  
     • Source control & CI (green)  
     • Publishing & docs (orange)  
     • External services (red)  

8. Detailed capture of essential elements  
   - Label each algorithm folder cluster inside the “Code Modules” box (e.g., Arrays, Graph, DP, …).  
   - Inside “Documentation” box, show README.md + per-folder READMEs.  
   - If you introduce a CI node, annotate which steps run (compile, test, doc-gen).  

By following these instructions, your system-design diagram will accurately reflect the static-content nature of Interview_DS_Algo, together with its development workflow and external integrations—providing clarity to any principal engineer reviewing the project.  
</explanation>
